speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to determine the underlying cause, could you describe exactly how your walking and coordination have been affected?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk-like" appearance and right-sided clumsiness suggest cerebellar involvement. To narrow this down, have you noticed any specific symptoms like slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, or numbness in your hands and feet?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

The combination of subacute gait/limb ataxia, a history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, and the specific symptom progression strongly suggests JC virus reactivation. I will proceed with diagnostic testing to confirm.
